Notes on how this was derived:

- **Project "jobs"** has 12 issues. Six have `count >= 100`; the other six (JOBS-7 with 97, JOBS-8 with 88, JOBS-9 with 75, JOBS-A with 64, JOBS-B with 41, JOBS-C with 23) were excluded. Status was not used as a filter, so resolved/ignored issues would have been included had they qualified — none did.
- **latestRelease** is the release of the newest event by `timestamp`. JOBS-1 had two events (`jobs@2.1.0` on 2026-10-17, `jobs@2.0.3` on 2026-10-16), so it resolved to `jobs@2.1.0`. JOBS-3 through JOBS-6 have no recorded events at all, hence `null`.
- Sorted by `count` descending. Nothing was written or changed — only `listIssues` and `listIssueEvents` reads were performed.

One caveat worth flagging: the four `null` releases are not the same situation as "newest event has no release" — those issues simply returned zero events from `listIssueEvents`. The spec asks for `null` "if it has none," which covers this, but if you expected event history to exist for those issues, the events endpoint may be truncating or they may predate retention.
